question: True or false: a well-known Civil War photograph of General Grant on horseback was assembled from three separate photographs?
answer: True. Library of Congress staff found Grant's head set on the body of another general, Alexander McCook, on McCook's horse, in front of a background of Confederate prisoners at Fisher's Hill. It gave buyers the heroic picture no camera had taken. Photographs were cut and pasted long before computers; only the tools have changed.
move: Assume any picture may be edited, however old, until shown otherwise.
ask: Which old photos or documents do I trust just because they look old and official?
trap: False, because faking photos sounds like a computer-age problem.
reference: Mia Fineman, Faking It: Manipulated Photography Before Photoshop, Metropolitan Museum of Art, 2012
